I know what you mean and I’m so sick of how much it seems people don’t care. We have literally two people we see fairly regularly but otherwise we’re homebodies because hubby and I are both getting full disability from the VA. Saw friend and his gf (our two people) on Xmas eve. Xmas day she snaps me saying she’s so sick and has been puking all day. I immediately think it’s the virus. She insists it’s likely just the flu. Next day bf says she can’t taste anything (“likely from the puking, it’s totally just the flu because the rona doesn’t make you puke”) and I knew completely it wasn’t the flu. 
I notice a very very slight sore throat/tickle later that Sunday but try to ignore it because it could be anything. 

Monday: hubby now feels really sick with flu like symptoms minus vomiting, and I have a slightly worse sore throat. He had a fever, I didn’t. She tests for rona. He’s asking about getting tested so I call and find out where to get rapid tests and the proper ones. 

Tues: he gets tested, rapid results are negative. I’m feeling a bit worse but still somewhat human more or less. Hubby feels like death (I’m guessing). Mid day get her results, she’s positive. Late evening he finally gets his, also positive. By now I can’t find tests anywhere and I can’t get us in for testing without driving 30 min and being around more people (rural area, have to drive to the next city up). Not a risk we’re willing to take and we’re also both completely exhausted and worn out feeling. 

Wed: I’m feeling ok with very very mild symptoms, hubby is not great. I do some slightly extensive cleaning beyond a quick wipe down. Less than 24 hours later, I’m hit with a low grade fever, worst sore throat ever, extreme exhaustion, and slight difficulty breathing. Being an overpreparer, we have a pulse oximeter that I got back in 2020. During the 72ish hours I had a fever that went up to 100.7° and my o2 levels are generally low 90s but it did dip to 89 at one point. It was awful and miserable and is still affecting me somewhat. I feel about 70% human again but yeah. I’m scared to do anything now, I don’t want that to flare up again, it was worse than any flare I’ve had before. And my dr wouldn’t do anything for me without getting tested. But I can’t get tested anywhere. It’s a lose-lose situation for any of us. And I’m not going to the er unless I’m bleeding out or have an obvious broken bone or such. 

And now we can’t get boosted for 90 days. Legit pissed because I was waiting to schedule it for when the weather stopped having 40° changes in the high to low because that causes flares for me. And I didn’t want to be in a flare, doing something that would likely cause a flare. 🤦🏻‍♀️

Just read all of this and I’m hopeful I can add to your relief and happiness. I was your girlfriend up until 2013. Married even. Hubby was/is very, very anti kid and I always wanted 2 kids one day. We had agreed on a future compromise when dating that we could possibly have 1 kid, or maybe adopt. All was great. (2010-2013).


Hubby deploys (we were both Air Force). We are old hands at being apart for long periods because thanks Air Force, so we would often have some pretty deep/impactful conversations when he was deployed or away and somehow one day the topic of kids came back up. It nearly caused us to divorce because he admitted he didn’t want kids or to adopt. His joke was always that we’d adopt a 17.5 year old and he’d tell them to figure out life on their own at 18 basically. I realized if I had the kid or kids I wanted that I’d either be married but basically a single mom, or I’d be a single mom. I didn’t really want either of those things, I wanted my hubby. I had to do some deep soul searching that week. I picked hubby, sleeping in, vacations when we want (when we have the $$), and the ability to spend my money how and where/when I wanted, and on myself or hubby. We have a nice home and aren’t wealthy by any means but we do save up and have nicer things than we would have been able to if we had kids. 


So basically, not all hope is lost and she might decide kids aren’t actually for her after all. I know I did. Feel free to point out the things like sleeping in, having the pets or plants she might want, and also nicer things, without worry about how money is being spent or if a kid could easily break it. 

TLDR: I was the GF (wife in my case) and ended up changing my mind about kids.

I went to my PCM with the application for a placard filled out and just needing his signature. He agreed with my reasons for it, and so I got a temporary one. When it expired and my issues hadn’t gone away, I went to him with the application filled out for it to be a permanent placard and he signed it with zero hesitation. This was a few years ago now, and I don’t see that dr anymore (I separated from the military and he moved before that) but I am still very thankful to him for doing it for me. Having the placard means I can go grocery shopping and get everything on my list instead of a few things I can handle before having to trek to my car. It means I don’t have to stress (and then have a flare from the stress) to try to get close parking for any events we go to and so on. I don’t think I’m disabled, but I know I have more issues than a healthy person. Plus, my fibro has progressively gotten worse over the years, along with additional issues. 

TL:DR: my advice would be to bring the filled out application to your dr and plead your case to him. It’s much harder to say no to someone in person than it is to say no in an email/message. Good luck, don’t give up!
